name: Mewmaxxing

lead: Mewmaxxing is the pairing of two habits: mewing, a tongue-posture routine, and nasal breathing with the mouth closed. Practitioners hope that the combination improves jaw, chin and cheekbone definition over time and gives a more structured profile.

Mewing comes from the orthotropics work of orthodontist John Mew and his son Mike. Nasal breathing is a broadly recognised healthy breathing route. The two ideas are combined in forum discussion, but no published trial has tested the combined routine for facial appearance.

paras: In general terms, people rest the tongue against the roof of the mouth, keep the lips closed and breathe through the nose during the day, and some also try to keep the mouth closed during sleep. It is a posture habit rather than a product, and forum users typically describe following it for months or years.

The routine involves no drugs or devices, and nasal breathing itself is generally considered normal healthy breathing. Discussion of mewing in the media has noted that orthodontic bodies see no evidence it reshapes adult jaws, and that Mike Mew was struck from the UK dental register in 2024 over his treatment of children. Persistent nasal obstruction is a medical matter for a clinician.

chain: Mouth stays closed with nasal breathing
Practitioners hope for a more defined jaw and midface over time
angle.text: Practitioners use mewmaxxing hoping for a more defined jawline, chin and midface and a less slack lower face. The routine is free and involves holding a posture through the day, often alongside chewing, skin care and body-fat reduction.

lead: Mewmaxxing is a looksmaxxing term for combining mewing with nasal breathing. Mewing is a practice of resting the tongue on the roof of the mouth, and nasal breathing means keeping the lips closed and breathing through the nose. Practitioners present the pair as a free, non-surgical way to work toward a sharper jawline, better chin projection and a more forward midface.[1]

Mewing is named after British orthodontist John Mew, who developed it within a system called orthotropics together with his son Mike.[1] Interest rose from about 2019, driven by social media and looksmaxxing communities.[1] Nasal breathing is a separate, widely described normal breathing pattern in which the nose warms, moistens and filters incoming air.[2] Mewmaxxing treats the two as complementary: the tongue posture is said to shape the palate and jaw, and a closed mouth is said to keep the tongue in place.

Research and expert views are attributed in the sections below. Orthodontic bodies such as the American Association of Orthodontists report no evidence that mewing improves the jaw, and most orthodontists do not regard it as a substitute for orthognathic surgery.[1] No published trial has examined mewmaxxing as a combined practice.

paras: Mewmaxxing is not a single formal method. It is the community habit of doing mewing and nasal breathing together, with the "maxxing" suffix signalling an effort to optimise the routine. Mewing involves positioning the tongue against the palate.[1] Nasal breathing involves keeping the mouth closed so air passes through the nose, where mucosa warms, humidifies and filters it.[2]

Proponents say a tongue resting on the palate provides gentle, constant force that influences the upper jaw and face, and that mouth breathing lets the tongue drop and the face "elongate". They therefore treat nasal breathing as the enabling half of the routine. These are practitioner beliefs rather than findings from trials.[1]

Wikipedia reports that no credible research has shown orthotropics works, that the American Association of Orthodontists reports no evidence mewing improves the jaw, and that most orthodontists do not treat it as a replacement for jaw surgery.[1] Separately, the nasal breathing literature describes functions of the nose such as warming, humidifying and filtering air, and one 2023 study cited there linked acute nasal breathing in young adults with lower diastolic blood pressure.[2] The sources do not link breathing route to adult facial shape.
Mike Mew was expelled from the British Orthodontic Society and faced a misconduct hearing over harm to child patients, and in 2024 was struck from the UK dental register.[1]
No studies found. No published trial has tested mewing combined with nasal breathing for facial appearance.

lore.intro: In looksmaxxing communities, mewmaxxing is discussed as the complete version of mewing, with nasal breathing and mouth taping often named alongside tongue posture.

claims.claim: Nasal breathing keeps the tongue on the palate and so makes mewing work

timeline.event: Mewing interest rises sharply on social media.[1]
Mike Mew is struck from the UK dental register.[1]
